lineage: TTP overlap with CryLock (suspected successor, per Unit 42); infrastructure wiped and leak site defaced by the Ukrainian Cyber Alliance in October 2023
summary: Trigona was a 2022-2023 double-extortion operation that got in by brute-forcing poorly managed MS-SQL servers (then loading a CLR shell inside SQL Server), exploiting ManageEngine CVE-2021-40539, or buying access from brokers. Operators created backdoor admin accounts, set Sticky Keys debugger backdoors, opened RDP, dumped credentials with Mimikatz, scanned with NetScan/Advanced Port Scanner and used Splashtop to spread tools. A turnoff.bat script stopped 100+ services, cleared logs and deleted shadow copies before AES encryption with a .\_locked extension and an HTA ransom note. The Ukrainian Cyber Alliance wiped its servers in October 2023, and no reliable 2024-2026 TTP reporting was found.
uniqueTraits: CLR assembly shell loaded inside MS-SQL (sqlservr.exe drops svcservice.exe) with MS16-032 privilege escalation
Sticky Keys debugger backdoor on sethc/utilman/Magnify/HelpPane (DC4.exe)
Splashtop used for lateral tool transfer and deployment
Password-protected, UPX/Inno-packed tool bundle (DC2.exe Mimikatz, DC6.exe Advanced Port Scanner)
HTML-application (.hta) ransom note with embedded JavaScript and Run-key relaunch

chain.procedure: Brute-force / dictionary attacks against internet-exposed MS-SQL servers with weak account credentials.

atomics.note: No MS-SQL brute-force atomic exists; SMB password guessing exercises the same failed-logon burst detections (local ART T1110.001 #1)

chain.procedure: Exploitation of Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus CVE-2021-40539 (per Arete, cited by Trend Micro).
chain.noAtomicReason: No local Atomic test exploits these CVEs; validate with vulnerability scanning / patch-state checks or a purple-team exploit range, not ART.

chain.procedure: Re-use of compromised accounts bought from initial access brokers.
chain.noAtomicReason: Logging in with purchased credentials has no ART equivalent; validate with identity-analytics detections (impossible travel, new-device logons).

chain.techniqueName: Server Software Component: SQL Stored Procedures
chain.procedure: Loads a CLR assembly shell into SQL Server that accepts operator commands like a web shell (system info, account changes, privilege escalation); sqlservr.exe then installs the ransomware as svcservice.exe.
chain.noAtomicReason: The local catalogue has no SQL stored-procedure / CLR assembly atomic (T1505.001). Validate with SQL Server audit logging for CREATE ASSEMBLY and sqlservr.exe child processes.

chain.procedure: The CLR shell escalates privileges via the Windows Secondary Logon Service flaw MS16-032, dropping nt.exe.
chain.noAtomicReason: Local T1068 atomics are BYOVD/driver-specific; none exercise MS16-032. Validate patch state.
